chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, who said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to me from Ali ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the family of Abu Sufyan killed Al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him), so Allah took away their sovereignty. And Hisham killed Zayd ibn Ali, so Allah took away his sovereignty. And Al-Walid killed Yahya ibn Zayd, so Allah took away his sovereignty as punishment for the killing of the progeny of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.آل أَبِي سُفْيَانَ: The family of Abu Sufyan, referring to the Umayyad clan
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Imam Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.ذُرِّيَّةُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The progeny/descendants of the Messenger of Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the connection between killing the progeny of the Prophet and the loss of political power in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-Amal, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) linking the specific loss of Umayyad sovereignty to the martyrdom of the Prophet's progeny, illustrating a pattern of divine retribution. This narration underscores the Shia theological view that political legitimacy is contingent upon justice towards the Ahl al-Bayt, as the caliphate was stripped from each ruler following the killing of a specific descendant.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 11.  Imam  Ja’far  Sadiq  (a.s.)  said  that  indeed  when  the progeny  of  Abu  Sufyan  martyred  Imam  Husain  (a.s.),  the Almighty  Allah  snatched  their  power  from  them.  When Hisham martyred Zaid bin Ali, Allah took away power from him also. Similarly when Walid martyred Yahya bin Zaid, the Almighty Allah took away his power as punishment.
